--- title: "Multiple linear regression" subtitle: "Types of predictors cont'd" date: "September 10, 2026" author: Shane Rybacki date-format: "MMMM DD, YYYY" footer: "[🔗 sta221-fa26.github.io](https://sta221-fa26.github.io)" logo: "../images/logo.png" format: revealjs: theme: slides.scss multiplex: false transition: fade slide-number: true incremental: false chalkboard: true include-before: [ ''] html: output-file: 06-predictor-types-notes.html html-math-method: method: mathjax url: "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mathjax@3/es5/tex-mml-chtml.js" execute: freeze: auto echo: true knitr: opts_chunk: R.options: width: 200 bibliography: references.bib --- ## Announcements \[UPDATE\] ## Topics - Interaction terms - Higher order terms - Model comparison ## Computing setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # load packages library(tidyverse) library(tidymodels) library(openintro) library(patchwork) library(knitr) library(kableExtra) library(PNWColors) # for color palette # set default theme and larger font size for ggplot2 ggplot2::theme_set(ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 16)) ``` ::: ## Data: Lemurs ::: {.cell} ::: ::: midi Today’s data contains a subset of the original Duke Lemur data set available in the [TidyTuesday GitHub repo](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/master/data/2021/2021-08-24/readme.md). This data includes information on 252 lemurs less than 24 months old from three taxa: - Eulemur rufus (ERUF), commonly known as Red-fronted brown lemur - Propithecus coquereli (PCOQ), commonly known as Coquerel’s sifaka - Varecia rubra (VRUB), commonly known as Red ruffed lemur. ::: :::::: columns ::: {.column width="33%"} ![ERUF](images/06-eruf-lemur.jpg){fig-align="center"} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![PCOQ](images/06-pcoq-lemur.jpg){fig-align="center"} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![VRUB](images/06-vrub-lemur.png){fig-align="center"} ::: :::::: ::: small Images from [Duke Lemur Center - Meet the Lemurs](Duke%20Lemur%20Center.%20n.d.%20“Meet%20the%20Lemurs.”%20https://lemur.duke.edu/discover/meet-the-lemurs/) ::: ## Variables **Predictors**: - `taxon` : Code made as a combination of the lemur’s genus and species. Note that the genus is a broader categorization that includes lemurs from multiple species. (`ERUF`: Eulemur rufus, `PCOQ`: Propithecus coquereli, `VRUB`: Varecia rubra) - `age`: Age of the lemur when weight was recorded (in months) - `litter_size`: Total number of infants in the litter the lemur was born into (this includes the observed lemur) **Response**: `weight`: Weight of the lemur (in grams) ## Response vs. predictors ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](07-predictor-types-contd_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: . . . **Goal**: Use age, taxon, and litter size to understand variability in the weight of lemurs younger than 24 months old. ## Model fit in R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lemur_fit <- lm(weight ~ age + taxon + litter_size, data = lemurs) tidy(lemur_fit) |> kable(digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |term | estimate| std.error| statistic| p.value| |:-----------|--------:|---------:|---------:|-------:| |(Intercept) | -0.772| 116.993| -0.007| 0.995| |age | 137.479| 4.845| 28.377| 0.000| |taxonPCOQ | 462.184| 95.287| 4.850| 0.000| |taxonVRUB | 1020.390| 133.468| 7.645| 0.000| |litter_size | -14.101| 65.756| -0.214| 0.830| ::: ::: ::: question - Write the regression equation for ERUB lemurs. - Write the regression equation for PCOQ lemurs. ::: ## Growth rate by taxon ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tidy(lemur_fit) |> select(term, estimate) |> kable(digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} |term | estimate| |:-----------|--------:| |(Intercept) | -0.772| |age | 137.479| |taxonPCOQ | 462.184| |taxonVRUB | 1020.390| |litter_size | -14.101| ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} - In the current model, the growth rate (effect of age) is the same for all observations - We wish to explore whether the growth rate differs by taxon - To do so, we will add an interaction effect between `age` and `taxon` ::: ::::: ## EDA for interaction effect ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](07-predictor-types-contd_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){fig-align='center' width=960} ::: ::: ::: question - How do we expect the lines to compare if there is [**no**]{.underline} interaction effect? - How do we expect the lines to compare if there [**is**]{.underline} an interaction effect? ::: ## Interaction terms - Sometimes the relationship between a predictor variable and the response depends on the value of another predictor variable. - This is an **interaction effect**. - To account for this, we can include **interaction terms** in the model. ## Your turn \[UPDATE\] ::: question We wish to fit of the variability in lemur weight using `age`, `taxon`, `litter_size`, and the interaction between `age` and `taxon`. What are the dimensions of the design matrix $\mathbf{X}$? ::: \[MAKE WOOCLAP POLL\] ## Model with interaction terms {.smaller} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} lemur_fit_int <- lm(weight ~ age + taxon + litter_size + age * taxon, data = lemurs) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
term estimate std.error statistic p.value
(Intercept) 529.072 130.926 4.041 0.000
age 79.974 9.915 8.066 0.000
taxonPCOQ -361.629 134.561 -2.687 0.008
taxonVRUB 634.483 163.006 3.892 0.000
litter_size -32.108 58.649 -0.547 0.585
age:taxonPCOQ 95.760 12.076 7.930 0.000
age:taxonVRUB 47.649 11.924 3.996 0.000
````` ::: ::: ## Model with interaction terms ::: question - Write the estimated regression equation for lemurs from the `ERUB` taxon. - Write the estimated regression equation for lemurs from the `PCOQ` taxon. ::: ## Interpreting interaction terms Let's look at the coefficient of `age:taxonPCOQ = 95.760` ::: incremental - **What the interaction means**: The effect of age is 95.760 grams per month greater for PCOQ lemurs compared to ERUB lemurs. - **Interpreting `age` for PCOQ lemurs**: For each additional month in a PCOQ lemur's age, their weight is expected to be greater by 175.734 (79.974 + 95.760) grams, on average, holding litter size constant. - In short, the growth rate of young PCOQ lemurs is 175.734 grams per month. ::: ## Indicators and interactions ::: question In general, how do - indicators for categorical predictors impact the model equation? - interaction terms impact the model equation? ::: ## Higher-order terms We may consider - do something with age sq. - does thi smodel make sense in practice? # Model comparison ## Model evaluation: RMSE & $R^2$ - **Root mean square error, RMSE**: A measure of the average error (average difference between observed and predicted values of the outcome) - **R-squared**, $R^2$ : Percentage of variability in the outcome explained by the regression model ## Comparing models {.small} Let's consider the following models: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |term | Model 1| Model 2| |:-------------|--------:|--------:| |(Intercept) | -0.772| 529.072| |age | 137.479| 79.974| |taxonPCOQ | 462.184| -361.629| |taxonVRUB | 1020.390| 634.483| |litter_size | -14.101| -32.108| |age:taxonPCOQ | NA| 95.760| |age:taxonVRUB | NA| 47.649| ::: :::
**How do we decide which model to choose?**
## Comparing models - When comparing models, do we prefer the model with the lower or higher RMSE? - Though we use $R^2$ to assess the model fit, it is generally unreliable for comparing models with different number of predictors. Why? - $R^2$ will stay the same or increase as we add more variables to the model. - If we only use $R^2$ to choose a best fit model, we will be prone to choose the model with the most predictor variables. ## Adjusted $R^2$ - **Adjusted** $R^2$: measure that includes a penalty for unnecessary predictor variables - Similar to $R^2$, it is a measure of the amount of variation in the response that is explained by the regression model - Use the `glance()` function to get $Adj. R^2$ in R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} glance(lemur_fit)$adj.r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.7988424 ``` ::: ::: ## $R^2$ and Adjusted $R^2$ $$R^2 = \frac{SSM}{SST} = 1 - \frac{SSR}{SST}$$
. . . $$R^2_{adj} = 1 - \frac{SSR/(n-p-1)}{SST/(n-1)}$$ where - $n$ is the number of observations used to fit the model - $p$ is the number of non-intercept terms in the model ## Using $R^2$ and Adjusted $R^2$ - Adjusted $R^2$ can be used as a quick assessment to compare the fit of multiple models; however, it should not be the only assessment - Use $R^2$ when describing the relationship between the response and predictor variables ## Comparing models ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} **Model 1** **Model without interaction** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # r-squared glance(lemur_fit)$r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.8020481 ``` ::: :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # adj-r-squared glance(lemur_fit)$adj.r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.7988424 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} **Model 2** **Model with interaction** ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # r-squared glance(lemur_fit_int)$r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.8443483 ``` ::: :::
::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # adj-r-squared glance(lemur_fit_int)$adj.r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.8405364 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::::: ## Recap - Interaction effects - Quadratic effects - Model comparison ## Before next class - Complete [Lecture 08 prepare](../prepare/prepare-lec08.html): Inference for regression

  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
